$comment: One shared truth table for turning a stored key into owner-facing words. Read by the TypeScript resolver test (hushh-webapp/__tests__/lib/humanize-segment.test.ts) and the Python one (consent-protocol/tests/test_pkm_manifest_scope_labels.py). Two implementations that must agree need one list of truths, or they drift the way the twelve humanizers this replaced did.

segments.why: The camelCase boundary is what scope-path lowercasing destroys. This is the case that made a chat row read 'Saved Places Locations Items Addressdetails Buildingcolor'.
Same boundary, second segment of the same real path.
Top-level domain segment written by the live location writer.
A letter run into digits reads as a machine name. Titled itself 'Last4' on the owner's Memory screen.
Both boundaries in one key: camelCase and letter-to-digit.
Short codes must survive intact. The digit split requires three or more letters precisely so w2 and k1 are not broken apart.

Underscore separators still work. Critically this must NEVER shorten to 'Status': a previous last-word heuristic (splitScopeLabel, reverted by merge d3336b95e) did exactly that and changed the meaning of the field. This fixture encodes that rationale so the heuristic cannot be re-proposed.
An acronym followed by a word. The ordinary camelCase boundary cannot see this one.
An already-plain segment must pass through unchanged.

opaque_ids.why: A uuid is opaque whatever prefix precedes it. This one titled a saved card 'Card 94d850a3 A02c 414c 9813 A48e64b0fa53' on the owner's Memory screen.

not_opaque_ids.why: An ordinary readable key must not be suppressed.
Letters and digits are not an identifier.
An ordinary readable key must not be suppressed.
